title: GWAS-lite: many SNPs, one phenotype
dek: A GWAS is a mountain of association tests. The likelihood at each SNP is usually a GLM. The scientific objects are population structure, LD, and the error rate for the family of tests.
story: At one SNP, a typical model is g(E[Y | G, C]) = β₀ + β_G G + Cᵀγ, with G a dosage 0/1/2 and C a handful of principal components or a kinship matrix. That is a GLM you already know. The mountain is m ≈ 10⁵–10⁷ such tests, dependent through LD.

A Manhattan plot is a display of −log10 p against genomic position. It is not a likelihood. Genomic inflation λ_GC is a median-based check of whether the bulk of tests looks like the null χ² they claim. λ > 1 can be structure, polygenicity, or a bad test.

TB bacterial GWAS is not human GWAS with smaller n. Clonality, recombination deserts, and lineage-tagging SNPs make “independent tests” a fiction. Linear mixed models with a kinship matrix, or phylogeny-aware models, are the structure plates — not a Bonferroni of iid χ².
deepTitle: The per-SNP likelihood, and what the peak is not
deep: Score tests at each SNP (only the null GLM fitted once) are popular because they are fast. Wald/LRT need a fit per SNP. Rare variants with separation make Wald explode; use score, Firth, or a burden test that aggregates a window.
LD: a peak is a region, not a causal nucleotide. Fine-mapping and functional follow-up are extra models. Reporting the smallest p SNP as “the causal mutation” is a decoder-ring error.
Power: for a binary phenotype, n_cases and allele frequency set the game. A mutation at 1% in 200 isolates is a rare-event logistic, not a GWAS with 200,000 independent bits of information.
Hold out a phenotype, a lineage, or a country. A peak that dies on replication in a new lineage may have been a lineage tag. That is a feature of the data, not a software bug.

formulas.label: Per-SNP GLM
formulas.expression: g(E[Y | G, C]) = β₀ + β_G G + Cᵀ γ
formulas.note: G dosage; C structure covariates or a random effect with kinship.

formulas.label: Genomic inflation (median)
formulas.note: A bulk-null check. λ≈1 is not proof of no confounding at the peaks.

visual.caption: A cartoon “peak”: a window of SNPs in LD with a functional allele. The tallest mark is the smallest p in the window, not a proof of causality. Structure covariates belong in the GLM, not in the caption after the fact.

example.title: A lineage-tagging SNP looks like FQ-R
example.setup: A SNP present in 90% of L2 and 5% of other lineages. FQ-R is also enriched in L2. Per-SNP logistic of FQ-R on G without C: huge β_G. With lineage or PCs: β_G collapses.

steps.title: Unadjusted GLM
steps.body: The likelihood is Bernoulli in G. It is a real association. It is mostly the lineage fork, not a gyrA mechanism (unless the SNP is in gyrA).

steps.title: Adjust
steps.body: Put lineage or a kinship random effect in the mean / G. If the peak dies, it was structure. If it lives in gyrA QRDR, you may have a mechanism — still not a functional proof.

steps.title: Error rate
steps.body: Whether you Bonferroni or FDR the remaining tests is a contract. Do not Bonferroni the unadjusted scan and then tell a mechanistic story.

example.takeaway: The per-SNP likelihood is a GLM. The GWAS is that GLM plus structure plus a family-wise or FDR rule plus LD humility.

check.prompt: The SNP with the smallest p in a peak is:
choices: A lead marker in an LD neighbourhood; causality is extra scientific work
Independent of population structure by construction
check.answer: A lead marker in an LD neighbourhood; causality is extra scientific work
check.why: LD makes a mountain, not a pin. Structure can make a mountain of lineage tags.

check.prompt: median(χ²_obs)=0.91, median of χ²_1 is 0.455. λ_GC equals:
check.why: 0.91/0.455=2. Inflation. Could be structure or polygenic signal in the bulk.

whyWrong.0.91: The observed median, not the ratio.

check.prompt: On the locus track, the functional mark is not at the lead SNP. The plate is teaching:
check.figureHint: lead SNP vs functional? inside an LD block.
choices: LD can make the smallest-p SNP a neighbour of the functional allele rather than the allele itself
check.answer: LD can make the smallest-p SNP a neighbour of the functional allele rather than the allele itself
check.why: That is why peaks are windows. Fine-mapping is another model.
